name: law_firm_software_004_grant_portfolio_integrity_sweep
instruction: Run the grant portfolio integrity sweep, applying the firm's grant reporting cadence policy GRANT-REPORT-01 (in firm_policies), batched under the episode batch code (ops_meta), as of the episode date. Two integrity classes need repair: a grant application's client must agree with the client of the matter it is linked to; and each award's reporting_schedule is authoritative against the live grant_reports tracking rows -- the policy decides what is missing, what has drifted, and what must never be touched (waived reports are not owed). Then report: one ops_reports integrity summary row under report='grant_portfolio_integrity' carrying the consistent-application count, the live report count, and the on-schedule count; one ops_reports row per award under report='reporting_compliance' with that award's report total and its overdue count as of the episode date; and a point-in-time reconstruction under report='grant_schedule_history' -- for each of the firm's four most recent past calendar quarter-ends, how many schedule entries were already due by that date and how many of those were unmet at the time (the policy defines what 'owed as of a date' means, and the reconstruction may only use what the cadence policy says a historical date can see). No other ops_reports rows for this batch_code under those three report names may exist. Do not modify grant_opportunities, grant_awards, or grant_expenses. Every collection this task doesn't write to must remain untouched.

hazards.mechanism: grant_applications.client_id disagreeing with the linked matter's real client: 2 hand-authored (APP-2026-001/003) + 15 bulk planted (snapshot-confirmed total: 17); APP-2026-002 is already consistent and must stay unchanged.

AWD-2026-001's progress report due_date drifted from its schedule entry (+5d vs +90d, snapshot-confirmed) and 40 bulk awards carry two-entry schedules with missing reports (snapshot-confirmed: 41 awards with multi-entry schedules) -- both the create and the correct paths are exercised.
8 bulk grant_reports carry status='waived' (planted, snapshot-confirmed: 8) -- GRANT-REPORT-01 forbids recreating or re-dating waived reports; touching any of them = FAIL.

the stage-5 point-in-time reconstruction uses only schedule entries already due at each quarter-end -- an early error in the schedule reconciliation (stage 2) silently corrupts the historical unmet counts (far from the cause).

success_criteria.summary: Every grant_applications row whose matter resolves carries its matter's client_id (17 live-confirmed mismatches corrected, the rest untouched apart from that field). Every real award's reporting_schedule entry has exactly one live grant_reports row with the schedule's due_date; the 8 waived bulk reports stay byte-identical (never recreated or re-dated); created rows carry status upcoming. The integrity summary, per-award compliance rows, and the four point-in-time quarter-end rows are all re-derived from live end-state and confirmed two independent ways (raw-row filter and SQL GROUP BY) which must agree. grant_awards, grant_opportunities, and grant_expenses stay canary-identical.

checks.expect: client_id matches the linked matter's client on every resolving application
every schedule entry covered exactly once with the schedule's due_date; waived rows byte-identical
schedule-coverage and matching counts agree between raw-row filter and SQL
point-in-time quarter-end values exact (only schedule entries due on/before each quarter-end count)

checks.collections: all seeded collections outside blast_radius, including grant_awards

top_results: 2 CFR 200.328 - Revision of budget and program plans (ecfr.gov)
2 CFR 200 Uniform Guidance Grant Reporting Requirements (grants.gov)

uniqueness_searches.query: grant application client matter mismatch repair reporting schedule reconciliation benchmark task
top_results: Conflict of Interest and Client Matching in Grant-Funded Legal Work (nlada.org)

uniqueness_report.differentiation_note: Fuses a referential-integrity repair (application-to-matter client matching, 17 planted mismatches) with a schedule-vs-tracking-table reconciliation (create missing, correct drifted due_dates, never touch waived) and a point-in-time historical reconstruction whose counts silently corrupt if the reconciliation was wrong -- distinct from task 009's read-only grant dashboard and from every other repair task's mechanic.
